summary: Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Kurtis R. Schaeffer earned his MA at the University of Washington and his PhD at Harvard University under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp. He taught at the University of Alabama before joining the University of Virginia in 2005.
Active in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kurunegoda Piyatissa was affiliated with the New York Buddhist Vihara, serving as its head as attested in 1998.

Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Kwangsoo Park earned an MA from the University of Iowa and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He served as a professor at Wonkwang University, attested in 2020.

A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, Kyo Kano studied at Keio University, Kyoto University, and the University of Vienna. Kano held posts as an assistant at Kyoto University (attested 1989) and associate professor at Kobe Women's University (attested 2000).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Kyojun Shimizudani studied under Keijun Shimizudani and at Taisho University. He served as professor at Taisho University (1919; 1926–1945), head of Hieizan Junior High School, and chief abbot of Sensō-ji (~1952–1979).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kyoko Fujii studied at the University of Tokyo. She served as professor at Hokkaido University (~1996–2008) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2008–2018), and president of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~2015).
Kyoko Tokuno is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held academic posts at the University of Oregon and at the University of Washington, where she was attested as a professor in 2017.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, Kyokuga Saeki trained under numerous traditional teachers, including Ryoga, Kasho Noyama, and Gen'yū. He served as the 143rd elder of Sennyū-ji from circa 1878 to 1888.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kyosho Hayashima held teaching posts at Yokohama City University and Toyo University (attested 1962), and served as a professor at the University of Tokyo, attested in 1980.
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Kyosho Tanaka studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1966 to 1974. He served as an associate professor at Musashino University from circa 1974 to 2017.
A scholar in Buddhist studies, Kyoshun Todo held positions at Bukkyo University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 1962) and later as a professor (attested 1988–1992).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology, Kyotaro Nishikawa studied at Keio University (~1948–1952) and served as Director-General of the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties from circa 1990 to 1997.

Kyozan Joshu Sasaki worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Zuiryō-ji under Joten Soko Miura, served as abbot at Yotoku-in and Shojuan, and founded the Mount Baldy Zen Center, serving as its abbot from circa 1971 to 2012.

Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Kyozo Yamada studied at the University of Tokyo and trained under Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani and other masters. He founded Kamakura Haku-un-kai in 1953 and became the second head of Sanbo Zen in 1970.

A Sinologist, Kōjirō Yoshikawa studied at Kyoto University from circa 1923 to 1926. He served as Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Kyoto University (~1947–1967) and as board chairman of Toho Gakkai (~1973–1980).

Active in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Kōken Unno studied at Nagoya University under Yoshifumi Ueda and Hidenori Kitagawa. He held posts at Nagoya University, Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music, and Meijo University (attested 2002).

Active in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, Kōshō Uchiyama earned a master's in Western philosophy from Waseda University and studied under Kodo Sawaki. He taught at Miyazaki Catholic Seminary (~1937–1941) and served as abbot of Antai-ji (1965–1975).
A scholar in Buddhist studies, Kōshō Ōtani studied at the First Higher School (~1929–1932) and Tokyo Imperial University (~1932–1935). He succeeded Kozui Otani.

Specializing in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Lajos Ligeti studied at Eötvös Loránd University and in Paris under Paul Pelliot. He held academic posts in Inner Asian studies at Pázmány Péter Catholic University and Eötvös Loránd University.
Lak La Sönam Chö Drub studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.
